messages:
elaine: Quick idea 1: run a 1-day "SI primer" with NeonTech + AccelOps focused on Private deployment telemetry. Objective: validate OTLP collector -> local Datadog agent relay -> dashboard import + a short joint press checklist. Interested?

mike: I can chair infra. We should confirm egress posture first (no-direct-internet vs proxy). Need to verify collector export paths and agent relay.

sam: I'll prep a tiny inference service (fastapi + simple opentelemetry span creation) and a k8s pod spec that uses nvidia.com/gpu. Will include a Dockerfile and a tiny load loop.

vijay: I'll invite partner engineers and get their SOC contacts. Also want to walk through marketplace listing implications: telemetry tile screenshots for the marketplace tile.

neontech-eng: We can join. We'll bring a sample SI collector config from our lab. One ask: can we avoid sharing real API keys during the session?

kevin (dd): Good plan. We can use agent-local relays + demo API proxy tokens. I can supply a dashboard template and a lightweight agent manifest. For tagging, prefer dd.tags like: env:prod, gpu_model:rtx4090, gpu_uuid:<uuid>.

sam: Collector example for relay mode (exporter points to datadog agent):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
processors:
  batch: {}
exporters:
  otlp/agent:
    endpoint: "http://datadog-agent.default.svc.cluster.local:8126"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp/agent]
```

mike: Note: for on-prem Private installs we often run agent as a DaemonSet with hostNetwork: true and a sidecar to surface GPU metadata. Plan: annotate nodes with gpu_model and gpu_uuid then have a small init container read node labels and inject DD_TAGS.

accelops-pm: We're good to participate. Can you share an agenda and a pre-req checklist (firewall, kube role, sample image)? Also we'd like to test trace sampling and top-level service mapping.

elaine: Draft agenda: 1) kickoff + security brief (20m) 2) deploy agent daemonset + collector (40m) 3) deploy sample model + run load (50m) 4) import dashboard & validate GPU tagging (40m) 5) blockers + marketplace screenshot capture (30m). Total 3h.

kevin (dd): Dashboard starter snippet (can import JSON): {"title":"inference-observability","widgets":[{"type":"timeseries","title":"p95 latency by gpu","query":"p95:trace.duration{service:inference} by {gpu_model}"},{"type":"toplist","title":"hot services","query":"top(avg:trace.duration{*} by {service}, 10, 'mean', 'desc')"}]}

sam: Security note: no secrets in plaintext in demo. We'll mount a k8s secret with a placeholder token and use a proxy token exchange script.

mike: I'll prepare a short egress-runbook: test endpoints (agent health, datadog intake if required), proxy env vars, ip ranges to whitelist for partner lab.

elaine: Action items:
- sam: sample app + manifest + make target `make demo-traces` by Mon EOD
- kevin (dd): dashboard JSON + agent DaemonSet example by Tue
- mike: egress runbook + node-annotation script by Tue EOD
- vijay: partner invites + SOC checklist by Tue

calendar-bot: elaine scheduled "SI telemetry primer: OTLP -> Datadog (Private)" Wed 13:00-16:00 PT 1 invite sent.

deploy-bot: CI: demo-app built successfully (ci/demo #789) image: registry/redwood/demo-infer:pr-22

neontech-eng: We'll prepare a short lab doc showing how we handle collector config in air-gapped sites.

accelops-pm: Sending SOC contact now. Also happy to help capture screenshots for marketplace tile.

sam: Example curl to push a synthetic trace to the collector for local testing:
`curl -X POST http://localhost:4318/v1/traces -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @synthetic_trace.json`
I'll add that file to the repo.

mike: Small utility to export node labels into DD_TAGS in the pod entrypoint: `DD_TAGS=\"gpu_model=$(kubectl get node $NODE -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.gpu_model}')\"` we'll add to the demo image.

elaine: Nice. Plan to capture a short joint announcement blurb after the lab if partners are happy. Keep it technical and not a marketing blast. Thanks all, see you Wed.
